Fracture healing is a complex process that involves several stages: hematoma formation, inflammation, soft callus formation, hard callus formation and remodeling

Many factors affect fracture healing , including the diet

And here we will talk about the 10 Foods that delay fracture healing

1. Alcohol

Alcohol interferes with fracture healing by inhibiting the proliferation and differentiation of osteoblasts

Osteoblasts are the cells responsible for formation of new bone

Alcohol also increase the production of inflammatory cytokines leading to prolongation of the inflammatory phase of the healing process

Laboratoires Servier, CC BY-SA 3.0 <https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/3.0>, via Wikimedia Commons

2. High Sugar Foods

Fast foods, deserts, sweets …

Foods high in sugar lead to high blood glucose levels which can cause inflammation and oxidative stress

These effects will prolong the inflammatory phase of the fracture healing process

formulatehealth, CC BY 2.0 <https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/2.0>, via Wikimedia Commons

3. Excessive drinking of Caffeinated Beverages

Tea, coffee, soft drinks …

High levels of caffeine promote calcium excretion in urine and impairs calcium absorption in the intestines leading to Delay in fracture healing

Panamitsu, CC BY 4.0 <https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0>, via Wikimedia Commons

4. Foods high in Salt

High amount of salts promote the excretion of calcium through the kidney leading to delay of the fracture healing

Dubravko Sorić SoraZG on Flickr, CC BY 2.0 <https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/2.0>, via Wikimedia Commons
